page: Amazon Web Services c6in.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 54 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the c6in.metal demonstrates strong multi-core performance. It achieves top-tier results in Passmark CPU testing, CPU extended instructions, and cryptographic encryption, alongside high performance in Geekbench ray tracing. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the server in the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is also a notable strength, with read-only cached speeds reaching 6700.46 GB/sec and uncached large-block read speeds of 335.16 GB/sec. However, single-core performance remains average, as evidenced by its middle-tier stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores.

The instance features a high-speed network interface with a baseline bandwidth of 200 Gbps, making it highly optimized for network-heavy workloads and Amazon Elastic Block Store connectivity. It does not include any local NVMe storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage must be provisioned externally. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal configuration provides direct hardware access and high resource density, making it a viable option for high-throughput network applications, multi-threaded CPU-bound tasks, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
